parts.name: Stator
parts.role: The fixed electromagnet that pushes the rotor around.
parts.whatItDoes: A stack of steel laminations with 24 wound teeth. Switching current through the windings makes each tooth a magnet in turn and pulls the rotor around.
parts.whyItMatters: On a heavy-lift motor the stator carries high current for long periods, so lamination losses and wire temperature class decide how long it lasts.
parts.material: Laminated silicon steel core with enamelled copper windings
buyingChecks: Winding wire temperature class is 180 C or higher
Ask for a thermal test at your hover current

parts.name: Rotor magnets
parts.role: Twenty-two permanent magnets bonded inside the bell.
parts.whatItDoes: Alternating north and south magnets that the stator field pulls on to turn the bell and propeller.
parts.whyItMatters: Heavy-lift motors run hot at hover, so the magnet temperature rating matters more than on small motors.
buyingChecks: Magnet grade and temperature suffix are documented
Ask for the magnet maker's certificate
